dnd-character-hud.description: DndCharacterHud — D&D 5e character HUD: the dnd-hero sheet atom rebound beside std ui-game-hud on one shared entity (HP hearts, LV, XP progress toward the next SRD threshold, AC). The hero atom stays the sole writer of the sheet; the HUD only reads.

dnd-dice.description: Headless D&D 5e dice authority: the SOLE writer of lastRoll + rollLog. Applies ROLL intents with structured {count,sides,bonus} specs (normal/advantage/disadvantage on a single d20), honors the deterministic rollQueue test hook (queue head per die, math/random fallback when it empties), and emits DICE_ROLLED. Renders nothing.

dnd-dungeon-board.capabilities: dnd dungeon board, tactical grid combat, floor delve, token art board, click to move, click to attack, descend stairs
dnd-dungeon-board.description: DndDungeonBoard — the playable D&D 5e floor: rebinds the six dnd atoms (dice, hero sheet, combat, dungeon-gen, token art, narrator) onto one shared entity and routes canvas clicks/keys into domain intents. START_DELVE carves a floor; FLOOR_GENERATED builds combat's ENCOUNTER_START payload (hero from config heroStats at heroSpawn, monsters from monsterSpawns through the monsterStats roster) and mirrors features into its own knownFeatures (server runtimes scope entity reads per-trait); click a monster to ATTACK, a reachable tile to MOVE, D/Space/G or the sidebar buttons for DASH/END_TURN/DODGE. Stepping on a chest rolls 2d4+2 healing (purpose loot → HERO_HEAL + CHEST_LOOT), stepping on a trap fires TRAP_SPRUNG (hero sheet rolls the dex save); each feature fires once per floor (openedFeatures). Descending the stairs regenerates deeper — unless it was config.finalFloor, which wins the run (result escaped + ESCAPED for the epilogue). The sidebar chronicles the narrator feed (tone → typography color), the last dice roll, the quest hook, and the action buttons.

dnd-dungeon-gen.description: Headless D&D 5e dungeon-floor authority: the SOLE writer of tiles, features, monsterSpawns, floor, heroSpawn. GENERATE_FLOOR carves 5-7 non-overlapping rooms joined by L-corridors (connectivity guaranteed by construction, verified by flood-fill with a deterministic single-room fallback), places stairs-down in the last room, heroSpawn in the first, and depth-scaled monster/chest/trap markers. Renders nothing.

kflow-chrome.description: kflow-chrome — the signed-in app shell, kept quiet for learners: a menu button opens the navigation (Home, New path, Import, Companion, Settings, the five most recent paths and the language picker), and the top bar carries only the brand, the suggestions bell and the account menu, around one content trait per page.

kflow-companion.description: kflow-companion — KFlow's learning companion: a chat assistant that reads the learner's paths and concepts and acts on them (create a goal, expand a level, mark a concept learned, add a note) through declared inputs that call the knowledge service, plus proactive suggestions (expand, study, review, connect, discover) the agent proposes on its own and the learner accepts or dismisses from the top-bar bell. Realizes std-agent-assistant (chat) and std-agent-suggestions (proposals): this file holds only KFlow's vocabulary, its tools, its owner-scoped records, the assistant's run history and the /companion page.

learning-algorithms.description: Algorithms learning app — orbitals are individual computer-science algorithms, each composed via `uses` from a per-algorithm engine atom on algorithm-canvas (bars/cells) or biology-canvas (graphs).

mesh-asset-catalog.description: MeshAssetCatalog — headless publisher that makes any mesh asset organism canvas-ready: INIT emits MESH_ASSET_PUBLISH { kind, states } where states maps anim state name (idle/walk/attack/hit/death/...) to draw-group items of draw-mesh descriptors authored in cell coordinates (z = height), each layer carrying its own keyframe animation — all pure config. Republishes on MESH_ASSET_SYNC so mount order against the 3D board's collector never matters. The 3D twin of SvgAssetCatalog. Renders nothing.

mesh-material-crystal.description: MeshMaterialCrystal — the 3D style contract's CRYSTAL recipe as a composable molecule: one draw-group applying the crystal rendering of the active style direction to any config shape. Where the 2D twin branches gradient+sparkle layers, this branches draw-mesh MATERIALS on the SAME geometry+palette: glossy (physical glass — transmission 0.8, ior 1.5, roughness 0.1 — the default, needs the rig's room environment to read as glass), flat (unlit basic fill), cartoon (toon bands + inverted-hull contour outline), neon (dark body driven by an emissive highlight with a default intensity pulse — pair with the neon rig's bloom), low-poly (glossy's transmission PBR with flatShading + the lowSegments tessellation — in 3D low-poly IS a token, standing in for the 2D twin's cutout/noir directions which don't apply to a volumetric mesh). Call sites override geometry + palette steps + style only; the recipes themselves are the molecule. Defaults derive from mesh-palette's style contract (arcane palette, materials.crystal preset).

mesh-material-gallery.description: MeshMaterialGallery — showroom for the mesh-primitives atom's PBR material recipes: a metal sphere, a physical crystal gem, an emissive magic orb (breathing on a slow float loop), a toon-shaded capsule with an inverted-hull outline, and a flat-shaded low-poly rock, all resting on one ground slab inside a room-lit isometric 3D canvas with a bloom pass — proving draw-mesh's material `kind` (standard | physical | toon) plus segments/flatShading/outline knobs render five distinct surface finishes off one shared primitive atom.

mesh-material-magic.description: MeshMaterialMagic — the 3D style contract's MAGIC recipe as a composable molecule: one draw-group applying the magical-energy rendering of the active style direction to any config shape. Where the 2D twin branches gradient+halo layers, this branches draw-mesh MATERIALS on the SAME geometry+palette: glossy (emissive-driven standard PBR core with a gentle idle bob+pulse — the default), flat (unlit fill, static — no default pulse), cartoon (toon bands + inverted-hull contour outline, static), neon (dark body driven by a brighter emissive highlight with the default bob+pulse — pair with the neon rig's bloom), low-poly (glossy's emissive PBR with flatShading + the lowSegments tessellation, still bobbing+pulsing — in 3D low-poly IS a token, standing in for the 2D twin's cutout/noir directions which don't apply to a volumetric mesh). Call sites override geometry + palette steps + style only; the recipes themselves are the molecule. Defaults derive from mesh-palette's style contract (arcane palette, materials.magic preset, motion.idleMs bob+pulse).

mesh-style-flip.description: MeshStyleFlip — the one-flip 3D style demonstrator, composed from the material molecules: the gallery row (iron metal sphere, arcane crystal gem, arcane magic orb, crimson unit-base scaffold, gold metal cube) rendered through the mesh style-contract token, with five buttons that flip the token live. Every embed keeps identical geometry+palette config; only style (plus the per-style lighting rig, post stack, and backdrop from mesh-palette's contract) changes — proving 3D art direction is a single token flip across all material-composed meshes (glossy | flat | cartoon | neon | low-poly).

mesh-units-crystal-golem.description: MeshUnitsCrystalGolem — volumetric crystal-golem unit: a low-poly faceted body capsule, a translucent pulsing crystal-head cone, and two small shoulder crystal cones, all built from flat-shaded draw-mesh primitives in the arcane palette — the 3D twin of svg-units-stone-golem, composed declaratively inside a 3D draw-host canvas.

mesh-units-flame-wisp.description: MeshUnitsFlameWisp — volumetric flame-wisp unit: an emissive core sphere bobbing and flickering, a smaller inner glow sphere, and a swaying cone flame tip, all built from draw-mesh primitives in the fire palette — the 3D twin of svg-units-flame-imp, composed declaratively inside a 3D draw-host canvas.

riya-game.description: Riya — a math journey GAME with real physics, structured as an app: a collection of orbitals, one per world, plus a menu. Riya is a dot, a point in space with MASS: the player pushes it with arrows / WASD (hold to accelerate — keyMap/keyUpMap on the math-canvas) or taps the d-pad (velocity impulses), and the std-motion-body authority integrates gravity, acceleration, speed, damping, and walls every 50ms. Seven worlds climb the math ladder: the number line (/riya-line — coast and brake onto the ★ numbers), functions (/riya-curve — riya rides y = 0.25x² − 4, the rule picks your height), the derivative (/riya-slope — the hill's slope pushes back through motion-body's bias field; park where slope = 0), the turning points (/riya-peak — a cubic's hilltop and valley, both flat spots of f(x) = 0.5x³ − 1.5x), the limit (/riya-limit — ride f(x) = 8/x toward the wall at x = 0 and watch the f(x) chip explode), the exponential (/riya-expo — the doubling curve 2^(x/2) − 1, flat then a rocket), and the integral (/riya-area — walk the strip, paint every column, watch area = … add up). Numbers are always on screen: tick labels on every axis and live HUD chips (x, v, f(x), slope, area) next to the ★ score, a velocity arrow on riya, and the tangent line under it on the slope world. EVENT HYGIENE (learned the hard way): the client runtime drains its actor queue in FIFO, so a per-tick event subscription floods it and everything lags — this game therefore keeps ticks SET-ONLY (motion integrates; the play trait's gameTick collects stars / paints strips / writes the hill bias directly onto the shared entity) and reserves events for sparse, meaningful occurrences: keydown/keyup thrust, d-pad impulses, a star collected (BURST + PROGRESS), the gate's GAME_END. Each world composes std-motion-body + std-objective-flow + std-fx-particles with events renamed per world; collection runs in the play trait's gameTick because std-objective-reach's contract is discrete HERO_STEPPED steps, not continuous motion (see Almadar_Std_Game_Gaps.md). RiyaMenuOrbital (/riya) is the shell: title plus a button per world that (navigate ...)s into it. Clearing a world pops its clear overlay; Next ▶ navigates to the next world's page — and the final world's overlay is the RIYA COMPLETE celebration, returning to the menu. CONFLICT LAYER (v5.1): every good game needs an obstacle, and in riya the obstacle is the math itself — the misconception made physical. The LIMIT world's pole is a hazard: cross the danger line at x = 0.85 and the asymptote flings riya back and takes the last collected ★ (inDanger edge-guard so one entry = one penalty). The DOUBLING world has an antagonist: a second motion-body (the ghost, labeled 2^n) steered by the gameTick toward riya with acceleration ghostThrust·2^(stars held) — every ★ you carry doubles its hunger; a catch costs the last ★ and teleports the ghost back to its spawn (ghostArmed re-arm hysteresis at rearmDistance 2 prevents chain-drains). The AREA world's final ★ is a concept gate: gray and uncollectible until all 16 strips are painted — you cannot finish before the whole sum is laid down. (Pages are mount-scoped in the playground runtime, so cross-page run state like a persistent star bank would need a persistence-backed entity — out of scope; each world's HUD tracks its own ★ score.)

riya-game-platformer.description: riya the dot escapes the rail. In riya-game she was a bead slid ALONG the graphs; here the graphs are the landscape and she runs and jumps across them on foot. Twenty-eight worlds, one per math idea, all composed from the std game substrate — platformer-body (run/jump physics, one-way AABB terrain collision, pit-fall signal, curve-skating) + objective-flow (win gate) + fx-particles — rendered through math-canvas so the axes, the numbers, and the world's own function curve stay visible at all times. The arc: 1) The Plain — the number line as flat ground with pits; x is a number you stand on. 2) The Ramp — a staircase rising 1 per 2 across; slope is how fast you climb. 3) The Valley — y = x²/16 sampled into bars; you drop into the parabola and jump back up its walls. 4) The Mountain — a climb to the one summit star: the local maximum, where the slope flattens to zero. 5) The Pole — the ground rises toward a chasm at x = 3 that swallows you: the asymptote, the x the world never touches. 6) The Doubling Stair — steps of 1, 2, 4, 8: each costs double, and the last wall is too tall for your legs unless you find the springboard. 7) The Gallery — a Riemann skyline: the bars ARE the function, and you walk across its area. 8) Shifts — the same valley moved right 4: (x−4) transforms the function. 9) Corner — y = |x|/2: the slope jumps from −½ to +½ at a point with no slope. 10) Inflection — x³: steep, flat, steep; the slope's slope flips sign. 11) Log — ln(x+7): a burst that flattens forever, forbidden left of x = −7. 12) Derivative — the ramp you skate IS world 3's slope, drawn beside its ghost. 13) Area — the shaded region piles up behind you as you run: integration. 14) Accumulation — a hill whose height collects a dashed bump. 15) Decay — exponential decay toward a floor you never touch (y′ = −ky). 16) Tail — 1 + 12/(x+12): an infinite tail whose area stays finite (improper integral). 17) Series — steps 1, ½, ¼, … that never cross the ceiling 2 (geometric series). 18) Taylor — a line and a cubic hugging the sine wave you skate. 19) Vectors — every tread is the same displacement ⟨1.6, 1⟩; walking adds vectors tip-to-tail. 20) Contours — the skyline is a slice of the hill z = 7 − x²/16, with level lines z = 2, 4, 6 behind it. 21) Partials — the plane z = 3 + x/4 + y/2 slopes ¼ under your feet and ½ in the dashed direction. 22) Gradient — purple ∇f arrows always aim at the summit of the gaussian hill. 23) Saddle — the pass is the trail's minimum and the cross-trail's maximum at once. 24) Volume — each column is one sum; the climb across is the second sum: ∬ f dA. Every world: catch every ★ to clear; fall in a pit and riya climbs back at her spawn with every star kept — no punishment, this is a beginner's mountain Each world is its own atom under riya/atoms (riya-level-*) owning its entity contract, knobs, and page; this organism only rebinds them.

riya-level-accum.description: riya level 21 · Accumulation — the hill climbs fastest where the dashed bump is tallest. Slide the bump and watch the inflection point move; grow the bump and feel the hill steepen. Skate the accumulating hill — catch 5 ★! Composed from std-platformer-body + std-objective-flow + std-fx-particles + std-pickup + std-tutorial-overlay, rendered through math-canvas so the axes and the world's own function stay visible. Rebound into the riya-game-platformer organism (menu + all eighteen worlds).

riya-level-area.description: riya level 20 · Area — the shaded region grows as you run right; every vertical strip you pass adds its height to the total. Skate the curve and fill the area — catch 5 ★! Composed from std-platformer-body + std-objective-flow + std-fx-particles + std-pickup + std-tutorial-overlay, rendered through math-canvas so the axes and the world's own function stay visible. Rebound into the riya-game-platformer organism (menu + all eighteen worlds).

std-algo-astargraph.description: A* pathfinding engine on algo-graph-canvas — Step expands the open-set node with the smallest f = g + h (straight-line heuristic to the goal); badges show a compact f=g+h readout, the goal node holds state goal until expanded, and once the goal is reached the reconstructed route's nodes and edges switch to state path. An open-set slot strip renders alongside, ordered by f, head highlighted. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (AstarTransport); the A* expansion lives in the sibling AstarSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one open-set expansion), LEARN_RESET (reseeds g-scores from the start node), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.AstarTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-algo-astargrid.description: A* shortest path visualizer on a walled grid — an algorithm-canvas expansion: Step pops the open cell of least f=g+h (Manhattan heuristic), relaxes its unwalled neighbours, and moves it to closed; every open/closed cell carries its g/h/f as corner text (g top-left, h top-right, f bottom-right) so the priority order is legible at a glance. Reaching the target walks the recorded predecessor chain and recolors the path. The Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the step clock come from the std-learn-transport atom (AstarGridTransport); the grid expansion lives in the sibling AstarGridSim trait, which transitions directly on the transport's LEARN_STEP (applies one open-cell pop-and-relax), LEARN_RESET (reseeds from the start cell), and LEARN_UPDATED (full-shell repaint) broadcasts — delivered by the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use — and owns the full-shell scene render (the transport strip is embedded via @trait.AstarGridTransport — one render authority per shared entity). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

Each slide leads with large centred text; a short drawing plays once underneath and stops. The deck is a state machine: one state per slide, NEXT/PREV arrows.

std-breakout.description:
Breakout — the classic paddle-and-bricks arcade game, composed by atomic design.
Mechanics live in atoms: std-brick-breaker (domain atom, ball/px/bricks/score/lives/result
authority) + std-fx-particles (std substrate, brick-shatter floaters). Rendering is
composed from std UI molecules: ui-canvas (drawables + keyMap) inside
ui-game-shell (HUD chip + game-over overlay). This orbital only binds the
pieces to one shared entity and routes raw key events into domain intents
(PADDLE_SET / RESTART).

std-brick-breaker.description: Headless breakout mechanic: the SOLE writer of ball + px + bricks + score + lives + result. A tick advances the ball one cell; walls and the paddle bounce it, bricks shatter on contact (score +1, BURST particle), a ball past the paddle costs a life and re-serves, zero lives loses the run, clearing every brick wins it. Applies clamped PADDLE_SET intents and RESTART. Renders nothing.

std-comment.capabilities: comments, comment on a post, reply, edit comment, delete comment, report a comment, flag a comment, moderation queue, conversation stream
std-comment.description: std-comment — comments on posts: write, edit, delete and view a comment, report a comment into the moderation review queue. Headless CommentRules and CommentFlagRules own the writes; the comments page views them.

std-evade.capabilities: evade game, chase ai, grid movement, survival timer, keyboard steering, restart
std-evade.description:
Evade — a 12x12 grid survival game, composed by atomic design.
Mechanics live in atoms: std-evade-chase (domain atom, units/heroHp/score/result
authority — hero + three corner chasers in one units[] array, single writer).
Rendering is composed from std UI molecules: ui-canvas (drawables + keyMap)
inside ui-game-shell (HUD chip + win/lose overlay). This orbital only binds the
pieces to one shared entity and routes raw key events into domain intents
(EVADE_MOVE / RESTART).

std-evade-chase.description: Headless evade-chase mechanic: the SOLE writer of units + heroHp + score + result. Applies EVADE_MOVE intents (steps the hero one cell, clamped to the grid); a 1s tick steps three corner chasers one manhattan-sign cell toward the hero (blocked by the hero cell and each other's cells), adjacency deals 1 damage (hero 3 HP), each survived tick is the score, surviving surviveTicks ticks wins, and dropping to 0 HP loses. Applies RESTART. Renders nothing.

std-fitness-bookings.capabilities: my class bookings, cancel a class booking, upcoming gym classes, member reservations
std-fitness-bookings.description: std-fitness-bookings — the member's own class bookings, each with Cancel booking. Design and flow only; creating and releasing a place comes from std-class-roster's rules.

std-integration-settings.description: std-integration-settings — the hosted Integrations settings surface (W4 Tier C): masked credential inventory, save/remove through the tenant credential store, and per-service connection tests, all through the kernel's `credential-*` effects (list is masked last-4 only; set accepts only declared credential names; values never render or log; the kernel refuses a caller whose @user.role is not an integrations administrator). Bind via `uses Settings from "behaviors/std-integration-settings"` on an OWNER/ADMIN-gated page — access predicates need the app's [identity] roster, so the binding organism owns the gate, never this atom. Wire form surfaces (service + env var + masked value inputs) to SAVE_CREDENTIAL / REMOVE_CREDENTIAL / TEST_CONNECTION; the default surface shows store status, the masked inventory count, and the last test result. TEST_CONNECTION checks credential presence only; to show a live probe, the composing organism listens to TEST_CONNECTION for a service on that service's own atom (e.g. CALENDAR_LIST_EVENTS with maxResults 1) and routes the atom's result and failure events to PROBE_PASSED / PROBE_FAILED { service, message }.

std-kekec.capabilities: kids coding education game, programming lesson adventures, Slovenian children's learning game
std-kekec.description: Slovenian kids coding game — learn programming through Kekec adventures.

std-kflow.description: std-kflow — KFlow, the signed-in learning app in English, Arabic and Slovenian (/ar, /sl), assembled from its page atoms: the knowledge-map dashboard, starting a new learning path, a path's levels of concepts, a concept's lesson with questions, notes and interactive visualisations, importing notes (by hand or with an AI that proposes and you approve), anonymous discussions with other learners and in-character chats with a concept's originator, settings, and the learning companion that answers in chat and proposes next steps from the top-bar bell. Every learning path, concept and lesson comes from the learner's knowledge base through the `knowledge` service. The public landing page is served at / (/ar, /sl); every app page needs a signed-in learner, and the landing page's calls to action open the /home dashboard, whose gate sends an anonymous viewer through the host's /login and back.

std-kflow-site.description: std-kflow-site — KFlow's public site in the KFlow brand theme: the landing page in English, Arabic (/ar) and Slovenian (/sl), every call to action opening the app's sign-in.

std-membership.description: std-membership — gym/club membership with tier, renewal, freeze, cancel. Listens for SET_STATUS so std-lifecycle can drive automated transitions. Exposes CRM-pattern knobs.

std-mesh-tactics.capabilities: turn-based combat, strategy gameplay, volumetric-rendered animated units
std-mesh-tactics.description: MeshTactics — pilot consumer of the canvas-ready MESH asset contract: composes the std-tactics-board-3d frame with four uses-imported mesh asset organisms (stealth operative + sentinel robot on the VRM bone rig, plus flame wisp + crystal golem). Each asset's Catalog trait publishes its anim-state art (MESH_ASSET_PUBLISH) to the frame's MeshAssetArtCollector; the frame paints per-row 3D draw-groups and drives idle/walk/attack/death purely from game state. Units carry empty modelUrl so the mesh branch renders them; an operative + a wisp vs a sentinel robot on a 3x3 volumetric grid; moved units yaw to face their heading (grid-tactics writes `yaw`, the board rotates the per-row group); terrain ships via seedArt with zero imports.

std-mindful-feed.description: std-mindful-feed — filters your own YouTube and TikTok feeds by mood. Every video tile is judged once, one at a time: a channel you always allow is shown, a channel you blocked is hidden, anything else is classified into the declared `categories` by the browser's on-device model. Your current mood decides which categories are hidden and which are blurred, with the reason shown on the tile. The panel lists what was hidden, with Show anyway and Always allow this channel; switching mood re-judges what is already on the page. Curate asks KFlow what you are learning now, searches YouTube and TikTok for each topic in background tabs, keeps the results the on-device model judges relevant (at least `minConfidence`) as picks, and opens a pick only when you click it. Runs as a Chrome extension (everything stays in your browser).

std-nata.description: std-nata — Nata, the creator and mentor studio of the KFlow learning family, in English, Arabic (/ar) and Slovenian (/sl): a person's own courses with a new-course flow, a workbench that opens one of their paths for AI enrichment they approve item by item, a course builder (modules, lessons edited in KFlow, publishing and inviting students), the mentor view of every student's progress with an At risk flag, and the Learning page where invited students accept a course. A creator creates new paths in place (kflow-onboarding's generator as a dialog) and reads and edits each concept's lesson in Nata (kflow-lesson). Everything is built on the learner's own knowledge paths through the `knowledge` service; sharing is kflow-sharing. The public home page is served at / (/ar, /sl); every app page needs a signed-in person, and the home page's calls to action open /home, whose gate sends an anonymous visitor through the host's /login and back.

std-nata-site.description: std-nata-site — Nata's public site in the Nata brand theme: the home page for creators and mentors in English, Arabic (/ar) and Slovenian (/sl), every call to action opening the app's sign-in.

std-pong.description:
Pong — the classic paddle arcade game, composed by atomic design.
Mechanics live in atoms: std-pong-rally (domain atom, ball/paddles/score/result
authority, with a built-in AI opponent) + std-fx-particles (std substrate,
paddle-hit floaters). Rendering is composed from std UI molecules: ui-canvas
(drawables + keyMap) inside ui-game-shell (HUD chip + game-over overlay). This
orbital only binds the pieces to one shared entity and routes raw key events
into domain intents (PADDLE_MOVE / RESTART). Single-player by default: KeyW/KeyS
steer your left paddle and the rally atom's AI drives the right paddle toward
the ball; set the PongMechanic aiEnabled config false for two-player, where
ArrowUp/ArrowDown steer the right paddle by hand. First to 5 wins.

std-post.capabilities: social feed, post, share a post, like a post, edit post, delete post, report a post, flag a post, moderation queue, public timeline
std-post.description: std-post — a public social feed of posts: share, edit, delete and like posts, report a post into the moderation review queue. Headless PostRules and PostFlagRules own the writes; the feed page views them.

std-rawi.description: std-rawi — Rawi, the doom scroll that teaches, in English, Arabic (/ar) and Slovenian (/sl): a full-screen vertical feed of one card per screen that grows with the learner. On first sign-in a two-step welcome asks what they are curious about and which kinds of card they enjoy; from then on Rawi's companion (a background agent on std-agent-suggestions) keeps the next cards written from those interests and from what the learner liked or hid: facts, explainers with a five-second check, mini games and simulations, whose instruments are built before the learner reaches them. Cards from the learner's own knowledge paths are mixed in when they have any, with right answers counting toward mastery and course progress (kflow-sharing). The learner likes or hides cards, learns more (a companion card becomes a new learning path through kflow-onboarding's generator; a path card opens its lesson inside Rawi), adds explore cards to a path, swipes through the rest of a path, and visualises a card. The Topics page changes interests, card kinds, which paths feed the scroll and the path-card mix; Your companion lists what it writes about, what is coming up and the liked cards. The public home page is served at / (/ar, /sl); every app page needs a signed-in learner, and the home page's calls to action open the /home feed, whose gate sends an anonymous visitor through the host's /login and back.

std-rawi-site.description: std-rawi-site — Rawi's public site in the Rawi brand theme: the home page in English, Arabic (/ar) and Slovenian (/sl), every call to action opening the app's sign-in.

std-service-marketplace.description: Marketplace: products, auth, orders, payments. Pick for multi-vendor storefronts.

std-service-research-assistant.capabilities: knowledge query search, cached result retrieval, generated report display, research assistant
std-service-research-assistant.description: Research assistant: knowledge queries, cached results, and generated reports.

std-tiktok-feed.description: std-tiktok-feed — TikTok's For You feed as a std-page-watch: every video on tiktok.com (LIVE streams excluded) is reported once as ITEM, as soon as its placeholder fills in, with its `title` (the caption), `channel` (the author) and `link` (absolute, composed from the author and the video id — the tile has no link of its own). The selectors follow TikTok's page markup; when TikTok changes it, only this file changes.

std-tiktok-search.description: std-tiktok-search — TikTok search as a std-page-search: SEARCH { query } opens tiktok.com/search in a background tab, reads the video results' `title` (the caption), `channel` (the author) and `link` (absolute), closes the tab and reports RESULTS. The selectors follow TikTok's page markup; when TikTok changes it, only this file changes.

std-vector-platformer.capabilities: platformer movement (run/jump), physics-based gameplay, vector-rendered animated hero
std-vector-platformer.description: VectorPlatformer — pilot consumer of the canvas-ready svg asset contract on a pixel-direct side-projection board: composes ui-platformer-board with the uses-imported svg-units-platformer-hero organism, all traits rebound onto one local HeroWorld entity. The hero's Catalog trait publishes idle/walk/jump/hit/death vector states (SVG_ASSET_PUBLISH, kind player); the board's SvgAssetArtCollector merges them and the player paints as a keyframe-animated draw-group scaled to the physics box, driven by @entity.player.animation.

std-winning-11.capabilities: trust-based relationship networking, psychological compatibility matching, team formation optimization, Dunbar's-number-scale contact management, relationship maintenance reminders, reconnect nudges, watering-due alerts, interaction history log, touchpoint notes, conversation log, contact segmentation, Dunbar circles, network segments
std-winning-11.description: Trust-based relationship intelligence platform enabling intentional networking within Dunbar's number (150 connections), psychological compatibility matching, optimal team formation (2-11 members), proactive relationship-maintenance reminders, per-connection interaction logging, and Dunbar-circle network segmentation.

studio-account.description: studio-account — the signed-in person's account settings page: the workspace style they build in (builder, designer or architect), their language, and the AI provider and model the generator uses by default. Each choice saves to the person's own row the moment it is made.

studio-apps.description: studio-apps — the Studio home: a beta notice, the signed-in person's projects in a left rail (open one to build it, delete one after confirming), and a centred prompt to start a new app from a sentence, with the closest installed solutions offered as chips while typing (a chip fills the prompt). A new app opens in its workspace at /builder/:appId; the workspace reports each finished build back here (APP_BUILT), so an app row always names the program it was built into.

svg-asset-catalog.description: SvgAssetCatalog — headless publisher that makes any svg asset organism canvas-ready: INIT emits SVG_ASSET_PUBLISH { kind, states } where states maps anim state name (idle/walk/attack/hit/death/...) to draw-group items authored in normalized 0..1 cell coordinates, each layer carrying its own keyframe animation — all pure config. Republishes on SVG_ASSET_SYNC so mount order against the board's collector never matters. Renders nothing.

svg-background-cavern-depths.description: SvgBackgroundCavernDepths — free-projection background: near-black vertical gradient cavern backdrop, obsidian jagged stalactites hanging from the ceiling and stalagmites rising from the floor, and an arcane-palette glowing crystal vein winding across the mid distance with a slow pulse, veiled by a translucent depth-haze band.

svg-background-dusk-ridge.description: SvgBackgroundDuskRidge — free-projection background exemplar: raw-pixel coordinate scene with a dusk sky gradient, a glowing sun disc, two parallax mountain ridge bands, and a dark foreground — proving projection free (px space) for full-canvas backdrops.

svg-background-storm-peaks.description: SvgBackgroundStormPeaks — free-projection background: brooding storm over jagged mountains, raw-pixel coordinate scene with an obsidian storm-sky gradient, a dim royal glow patch behind the far ridge, three desaturated-to-dark parallax peak bands (far/mid/near, atmospheric perspective), a flickering lightning bolt threading the far peaks, and two slow-drifting low cloud streaks — composed declaratively from SvgPrimitives + SvgShading atoms inside a draw-host canvas.

svg-cards-relic-frame.description: SvgCardsRelicFrame — portrait relic card frame: obsidian body with a subtle vertical gradient, a gold metal-recipe outer frame band with a slow gleam pulse and a 3px obsidian contour, four reused gold corner diamonds, a gold-keylined art window, a gold-stroked title-bar band, and a small centered crystal-recipe gem with a pulsing sparkle — composed declaratively from SvgPrimitives + SvgShading + SvgSilhouette atoms inside a draw-host canvas.

svg-material-crystal.description: SvgMaterialCrystal — the style contract's CRYSTAL recipe as a composable molecule: one draw-group applying the crystal rendering of the active style direction to any config shape. The style token picks the recipe branch on the SAME geometry+palette: glossy (off-center rimLight→highlight→midBase→ambientShadow radial gradient, glow shadow, pulsing white sparkle, ambientShadow contour — the default), flat (midBase fill + one rimLight shine dot), cartoon (highlight flat fill, big shine, thick 6px contour), neon (no fill — halo + bright glow strokes with the pulsing sparkle kept). Call sites override geometry + palette steps + style only; the recipes themselves are the molecule. Defaults derive from svg-palette's style contract (arcane palette, strokes.outer 3, motion.idleMs pulse).

svg-material-magic.description: SvgMaterialMagic — the style contract's MAGIC recipe as a composable molecule: one draw-group applying the magical-energy rendering of the active style direction to a config shape. The style token picks the recipe branch on the SAME geometry+palette: glossy (rimLight→highlight→midBase radial core, glow shadow, pulsing translucent halo, NO contour — the default), flat (highlight flat core + one rimLight shine dot, no halo/glow), cartoon (highlight flat core, big shine, thick 6px midBase outline — cartoon outlines even energy), neon (stroke-only halo ring + bright glowing core ring, pulse kept). Call sites override geometry + palette steps + style only; the recipes themselves are the molecule. Defaults derive from svg-palette's style contract (arcane palette, motion.idleMs pulse).

ui-arena-board-3d.description: 3D grid-tactics arena composing headless std mechanic atoms (chase-ai, fx-particles, round-flow) on one [runtime, shared] GameState with a single canvas render authority.

ui-debugger-board.capabilities: kids coding puzzle, spot the bug, debugging, fix the bug, program review, sequence debugging
ui-debugger-board.description: DebuggerBoard — Kekec Koda cross-tier fix-the-bug puzzle: Kekec's walk program has exactly K buggy steps. Flag every buggy step and no clean step, press CHECK, and win only on perfect precision AND recall; wrong checks cost a try and mark every step right/wrong, and running out of tries reveals the true bugs.

vim-mode.description: Vim keybindings for the studio's code editors — vim, vi, modal editing, hjkl, normal mode, insert mode. Composes the std-modal-editor generic (topology + vim-flavored config) over the studio shell bridge, and translates its neutral SET_MODE/EX_COMMAND vocabulary into the shell's STATUS/COMMAND/REGISTER_COMMAND surface. Full default bindings: mode entry (i a o O A I v :), operators (d y c > <), motions (h j k l w b e 0 $ ^ G { } %), x/X delete, p/P put, u undo, ctrl-r redo, r replace, ~ toggle-case, J join, . repeat, gg goto-start; SET_MODE re-announces on EDITOR_FOCUS so a newly focused editor's caret starts correct.

std-agent-assistant.description: std-agent-assistant — an in-app assistant that operates the running app for the signed-in user. Each section's floating button opens it in a side panel docked beside the page (std-panel-launcher; a side sheet on small screens), where the conversation shows every step the assistant takes live as it works; /assistant is the same conversation as a full page, in the app's own shell (pass `appName` and `navItems`); past conversations and what the assistant remembers open in place from its toolbar (Back returns to the chat), on either surface. One request flows down a chain of std agent atoms on the bus: the conversation (std-agent-session) SENDs → CONVERSE → std-agent-context bounds it → std-agent-memory adds what it recalls → std-agent-tool-loop answers it through std-llm's tool loop, firing only the inputs and reading only the entities its `tools` allow, as the signed-in user → ASSISTANT_REPLIED goes back to the conversation, to memory (remembered) and to std-agent-trace (the run record). By default the tools are the program's own declarations: every `-> external` input (its @description is the tool text) and a read over every persisted entity, so composing building blocks composes the assistant's abilities. Any section's page gets the assistant with two traits, `XAssistant = AgentSession.traits.AgentConversation` and a std-panel-launcher dock: the conversation speaks the ASSISTANT_* contract from any orbital, so the assistant needs no per-section wiring. Import the orbital once per app: `orbital Assistant = Agent.orbitals.AgentAssistantOrbital { config { instructions: "…" } }`. The conversation, memory and run records live in AgentRecordsOrbital; retarget them onto your own owner-scoped entities (`ownerId` a relation to your [identity] roster, with @read/@create) with `entities { AgentMessage: …, AgentMemory: …, AgentRun: …, AgentChat: … }`. The conversation is kept across pages and reloads (each person's most recently used conversation is the current one);

std-agent-completion.description: Takes a prompt, returns generated text through std-llm (LLM_GENERATE).

std-agent-context.description: std-agent-context — keeps what an in-app assistant sends the model bounded. COMPACT { messages } passes a conversation of at most `keepMessages` turns straight through as COMPACTED; a longer one has its older turns summarized with std-llm (LLM_SUMMARIZE) into one leading note and keeps the last `keepMessages` turns verbatim. If summarizing fails, the older turns are dropped and the recent ones still go through, with a visible warning — a summarizer outage never blocks the assistant. Headless. Nothing is persisted: the conversation itself lives in std-agent-session.

std-agent-pool.capabilities: behavior pool, shared generated content, retrieve by meaning, reuse generated behaviors, quality signals, retire bad content
std-agent-pool.description: std-agent-pool — a shared pool of generated behaviors that every user of the app draws from. WRITE { value, name, kind, topic, fields, description } takes a behavior already built and validated (a `program/eval` result), keeps its source durably (`behavior/source` → `program/print` → the `storage` service; the provider is the deployment's), embeds its description (`llm embed`) and records a PoolEntry; any failure on the way leaves no entry (WRITE_FAILED). SEARCH { vector, kinds, exclude, take } ranks the live entries of this pool by cosine similarity to the vector, nudged by their quality, and answers POOL_FOUND with the best ones, no model call. SIGNAL { id, signal } counts a play, like, hide, right or wrong answer on an entry and retires it once it has been played enough and most of its outcomes are hides or wrong answers. The pool name, kinds, bucket and key prefix and the quality knobs are config, so the same mechanism serves any app that pools generated behaviors.

std-agent-proposal.capabilities: agent proposal, review before commit, human approval of agent output, approve or revise agent suggestions, structured proposal review, ai drafts for approval, extract then confirm
std-agent-proposal.description: std-agent-proposal — an agent that reads what the person hands over, works out a structured proposal, and commits nothing until they approve it. The app starts it with PROPOSAL_REQUESTED { input, context } (any trait emitting it, or the person typing into the start form when `showInputForm` is on). A second std-agent-tool-loop answers with `instructions`, `prompt` and `tools` as the signed-in person — `quiet`, its reply and failure renamed PROPOSAL_LOOP_REPLIED / PROPOSAL_LOOP_FAILED so they never reach the assistant's chat — and submits its proposal through one declared input, PROPOSE (its @description is the tool text): a summary and a list of items, each a flat map of scalar values the app names. The person reviews it (the summary, the items drawn with `itemPattern` and `itemFields`) and chooses: Approve emits PROPOSAL_APPROVED { proposal } for the app to commit (the app owns the commit; this atom writes nothing); Revise sends their written feedback back to the agent, which proposes again; Discard emits PROPOSAL_DISCARDED. Cancel while the agent works aborts its model call and emits PROPOSAL_CANCELLED. A run that fails, or ends without proposing, shows its error with Retry and Discard. The panel renders into `panelSlot`. Import the orbital once per app: `orbital Proposal = Proposal.orbitals.AgentProposalOrbital { config { instructions: "…", prompt: "…", itemFields: […] } }`, restating `tools` with PROPOSE addressed by its local orbital name (`{ event: Proposal.AgentProposalWorkflow.PROPOSE }`). Instructions, prompts, item fields and labels are the app's vocabulary, declared in config.

std-anim-tick.description: std-anim-tick — sprite animation clock atom. Owns a global animation counter and exposes the current frame NAME (@entity.frameName = frames[counter % len]) every 100ms tick. Boards compose it via `uses` + a trait-ref rebound (linkedEntity) to the board entity; render-ui merges @entity.frameName onto the animated sprite's asset, replacing the inlined animTick frame counters that were duplicated across game boards. 1.1.0 redesign: the 1.0.0 units-frame-advance / effects-aging sets were removed — numeric unit frames served the pre-animation-contract regime (draw-sprite paints atlas sub-texture NAMES, which is exactly what frameName now exposes; zero consumers existed), effects aging is owned by std-fx-particles, and the shared-entity one-writer rule (ORB_SHARED_ENTITY_FIELD_CONFLICT) forbids a shared atom co-writing fields a board's own ticks also write. Tick interval is a language-level literal (100ms); the config surface is `frames`.

std-app-layout.capabilities: settings page shell, preferences page, account settings layout, profile settings, admin console shell
std-app-layout.description: std-app-layout — dashboard-layout chrome (sidebar nav + top bar with search + topBarActions + notifications) wrapping a single contentTrait slot. Use for list-style apps (CMS / helpdesk / CRM) and account/settings pages: the chrome stays stable while the consumer's content trait renders the data, and the consumer can add domain icons (cart / profile / help) via topBarActions. Bind once per orbital — the consumer rebinds linkedEntity via `XAppLayout = AppShell.traits.AppLayout -> XEntity` so multiple orbitals in one file each get their own chrome without colliding on a shared atom entity.

std-app-search.description: std-app-search — reusable global search: wraps a host content view and, on a SEARCH trigger, fetches the linked entity filtered by @config.searchField and renders the matching results, then CLEAR_SEARCH returns to the host view. Rebind to any entity; point @config.idleContent at the normal view and wire a trigger (e.g. AppLayout SEARCH) into SEARCH.

std-approval-gate.description: std-approval-gate — generic approval gate / approver workflow. Use when a user voices that an action must be reviewed, approved, signed off, or authorized by a privileged role before it proceeds (admin approval, supervisor sign-off, manager approval, gatekeeper review, editor approval, senior editor approval, reviewer approval, publishing approval, draft approval, content review, submit drafts then editors review and approve or reject, needs approval before going live, requires sign-off before publish). Persists ApprovalRequest rows + surfaces the PENDING ones in a review queue showing what is being approved and who asked, with Approve / Deny actions — Deny captures a written reason. approverRoles is ENFORCED by the review transitions themselves: an APPROVE/DENY from a viewer whose role is not listed does not fire. blockSelfApproval additionally stops a reviewer approving their own request (four-eyes) — DENY stays allowed as self-withdrawal. On approval emits ApprovalGranted; on denial emits ApprovalDenied (with the reason). Hosts that replay the gated action MUST route a failed replay back via APPROVAL_REPLAY_FAILED so the request reopens instead of being silently consumed. Compose onto any orbital whose action you want to gate: the target orbital emits an external event, an ApprovalRequest row is created (stamp subjectLabel/subjectId/requestedBy so reviewers see what they are judging), and downstream effects wait on ApprovalGranted. Differs from std-mod-queue, which is content-moderation-specific.

std-arcade-board-3d.description: 3D arcade-hall FRAME: composes hero-nav (free roam) + arcade-play (token/ticket economy) + fx-particles + arcade-flow (win/lose) onto one shared GameState with a single render authority. Games consume this molecule and supply only theme/assets/units/tiles/machines via config.

std-arcade-flow.description: Headless win/lose authority for the arcade play-for-tickets loop: owns only result. Listens SCORE_CHANGED (tickets + tokens) and sets result to won once tickets reach the target, lost when tokens run out first, else none. Renders nothing.

std-arcade-play.description: Headless arcade play-economy mechanic: the SOLE writer of tokens + tickets + machines. Applies a PLAY_MACHINE intent (spends a token, rolls a pseudo-random ticket payout within a configured range, emits BURST + SCORE_CHANGED). Renders nothing.

std-audit-capture.description: std-audit-capture — event-interceptor audit log / audit trail. Use when a user voices that a record's changes must be tracked, logged, or auditable (audit trail, track changes, change history, who edited what, mutation log, record changes, log every edit, edit history, modification log, who did what when, accountability log). Listens for the generic `EntityMutated` sentinel (rename via traitOverrides.events to the real mutation event, e.g. ContactSaved) and persists an AuditEntry row capturing actor, action, entity type/id, before/after snapshots, and timestamp. `captureEventTypes` filters on @payload.data.kind, or on the delivered event's own name when the payload carries no kind (empty = capture all). Every entry also records where the change came from — the delivering event, the behavior and module that emitted it, and the scheduled job when a tick caused it — with no change to the upstream emitter. Compose with `std-lifecycle` to apply retention. Composable via `extraTraits` to interpose audit logging behind any mutating trait.

std-avl-cosmic-zoom.capabilities: explore an app's orbitals and wires, drill into an orbital's state machines, play a transition step by step, see what an app imports
std-avl-cosmic-zoom.description: std-avl-cosmic-zoom — a whole app, drillable: the system map (one chip per orbital and the event wires between them, with a Dependencies lens over what each orbital imports), then one orbital's traits as state machines, then one transition as circuits. Step plays the transition on the kernel (`program/step`) and lights the machines and circuits with the run; a scene slider replays earlier steps. LOAD hands it the program to show (resolved) and the program as written (for its imports). Use for code workspaces and editors that let people explore how an app is wired.

std-behavior-catalog.capabilities: browse installed behaviors, search behaviors by meaning, describe a behavior's knobs and events, pick a behavior to bind
std-behavior-catalog.description: std-behavior-catalog — browse the installed behaviors under the `scope` registry folders (`behavior/catalog`), search them by meaning (the query is embedded with std-llm (LLM_EMBED) and ranked by cosine similarity to each behavior's description; results under `minScore` drop out), open one's knobs and events (`behavior/describe`), and pick one: PICKED { behavior, trait, value } carries the behavior name, its first trait as a value ready to bind, and the whole behavior as a value ready to embed or store. With `pick: toggle` each card carries an on/off switch instead: TOGGLED { behavior, checked, topic, value } per change, and SELECTION { behaviors } seeds which are on. Pick for block libraries, plugin pickers, plugin on/off settings and any page that lets users choose a building block.

std-billable-hour.description: std-billable-hour — generic billable-hour timesheet primitive for legal, agency, and consulting domains. Lists entries in `browsing`; opens entry detail in `viewing_single` with Invoice / Write Off actions.

std-cache-aside.description: infra atom — std-cache-aside (states: cached, empty, error, loading, stale)

std-crew-board-2d.description: 2D multi-unit crew-management board FRAME: composes hero-nav (unit-by-id move authority, no combat) + fx-particles onto one shared GameState with a canvas-2d render and select/deselect/move intent. Games consume this molecule and supply only theme/assets/units/tiles via config.

std-data-collector.description: std-data-collector — pure buffer-accumulation atom, parameterized for any ML domain. Collects data points into a buffer and fires BUFFER_READY with the full accumulated buffer once it reaches config.bufferSize, then resets for the next cycle. No ML compute, no model call — state machine + array operators only. Use ahead of a training loop, a batch inference call, or any downstream rung that needs a fixed-size window of accumulated observations.

std-escalating-decision.description: std-escalating-decision — the intelligence ladder itself, as one reusable composition. One request enters at DECIDE and falls through the rungs in order — R0 exact check, R1 table lookup, R3 retrieval, R4 learned inference, R5 generative classification — each rung handing off to the next by abstaining, until one proves the answer. Exits DECIDED, tagged with which rung answered (rung, confidence, matched, reasoning), or DECISION_FAILED if even the generative floor could not serve it. The escalation is a chain, not a hub: each rung listens directly to the rung above it and projects its own inputs out of the carried request, so the trait graph is a DAG and no event ever returns to a rung that already ran. Domain-agnostic: it knows about candidates and categories, not students or quizzes — grading, routing, matching, moderation, and duplicate detection are all this same molecule with different knobs. R2 (the Beta posterior) is deliberately not in this chain: it is the 'decide what to do next' half of a turn and already lives in std-knowledge-tracing.

std-graph-builder.description: Graph construction atom — builds node/edge structures from an entity collection for downstream GNN pipelines; pure array/object transform, no ML compute.

std-knowledge-tracing.description: std-knowledge-tracing — turns one true/false observation ('did the learner get this right?') into a tracked belief about mastery, and captures the same observation as a labeled training example in the same motion. Composes std-ml-posterior (the R2 statistical rung — a Beta-Bernoulli belief over an unknown success rate) with std-ml-label-capture: every posterior verdict — MASTERY_REACHED, REMEDIATION_NEEDED, or the abstain EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT — becomes a persisted labeled example (the input skill, the posterior's own verdict, and the ground-truth outcome that produced it), so a cheaper rung can later be trained to reproduce the same call without running the statistics. Domain-agnostic: it knows about skills and observations, not students, quizzes, or courses. One instance tracks one belief (e.g. one learner × one skill); the host composes as many instances as it has beliefs to hold.

std-multi-party-flow.description: std-multi-party-flow — Escrow.com / DocuSign / Stripe Connect style multi-party transaction. Header + summary (subject/amount/reference) + named parties (avatar/role/actor) + stage progress + your-turn panel + activity feed + dispute/cancel escape hatches. Topology = loading / awaiting / capturing_dispute / capturing_cancel / funded / released / disputed / cancelled / error.

std-stat-rows.capabilities: render a list/stack of stat rows (label + value) from a config-driven array; array/map over children; per-item @item field binding
std-stat-rows.description: std-stat-rows — a vertical stack of stat-badge rows rendered from a config-driven list. Exemplar for dynamic collection rendering over an arbitrary container: `(array/map @entity.rows (fn item …))` sits directly in a `children:` position, so no `renderItem` pattern is needed; the map lambda binds each row's fields with `@item.<field>`.

std-status-lifecycle-control.description: Status lifecycle control — infra molecule pairing std-status-lifecycle's StatusMachine, which deliberately surfaces no UI of its own. Pure presentational: shows the current status and one button per legal next move (config.transitions filtered on config.currentStatus), emitting ChangeStatusRequested with the picked move's id/from/to on click. Driven entirely by config (currentStatus/recordId/transitions) rather than a bound entity, so a host embeds it inline at the record it's viewing (currentStatus={@entity.status} recordId={@entity.id} transitions matching the paired StatusMachine's own config.transitions) and points that StatusMachine's `listens` at this trait's emit (`<Composer>.ChangeStatusRequested -> ChangeStatusRequested`) instead of at a dead declared-only event.
